open_points.subject: staff actor
open_points.question: Who counts as staff, how are staff distinguished from the owner, and are they trusted with the owner's host, configuration and vault access or only with the shared staff credential?
options: Staff are people trusted only with the staff credential
Staff have the same host-level trust as the owner
The owner is currently the only staff member
open_points.default_guess: Treat staff as human users who receive the staff credential but have no host, configuration or vault access.

open_points.subject: operator and model-provider boundary
open_points.text: “Operator — `onboard_object`, or an agent preparing a client message” and “every contact field it records or reads passes to the provider of the model the owner runs it on”
open_points.question: Is `onboard_object` always executed through a model-backed agent, or can it run directly without sending contact data to a model provider?
options: Every operator use is mediated by a model provider
The script may run directly; only agent-mediated use sends data to a provider
`onboard_object` and the model-backed agent are separate actors
open_points.default_guess: Treat the script and model-backed agent as separate operator modes, with provider disclosure applying only to the agent mode.

open_points.subject: trusted host processes
open_points.text: “Every process and container on Registry's host is the owner's and trusted”
open_points.question: What does “trusted” authorize: only unauthenticated API reads, or also direct access to the store, customer contact data and Registry configuration?
options: Trusted only to make credential-free catalogue API reads
Trusted to read the store but not configuration secrets
Trusted with all host data and secrets as the owner
open_points.default_guess: Trust host processes only for the explicitly open API reads; direct store, contact-data and secret access remains restricted.

open_points.subject: operator access to service tokens
open_points.text: “it holds no service token” and “could read the store and the instance's configuration, service tokens included”
open_points.question: If an operator agent reads a service token using the owner's host access, is it permitted to use that token and act as the named service, or must every operator action still use only the staff credential?
options: The operator must always use the staff credential
The operator may use any token readable through the owner's access
Token use depends on the particular operator task
open_points.default_guess: Require every operator action to use the staff credential even though the trusted agent is technically capable of reading service tokens.
